scope.renderer_predicate: teamBridgeEventOwnerConsent fires when every target is kind="agent" and target.account_id === actor.account_id (team-bridge-member-events-model.ts). That is the right test IN PRINCIPLE: a person IS an account (teamBridgeDirectoryMemberSchema keys a person by account_id) and an agent party carries its OWNER's account_id with its own endpoint_id, so same-account agents on an agent target are the actor's own. Two gaps are reported to the manager as source-side findings, not as locale defects: the predicate admits several targets while this copy is singular, and it does not require a human actor.

source_findings.current: {actor} approved their agent {targets} joining (singular "agent"); the sidecar asserts "{targets} is ... always exactly one name for this key"
source_findings.proposed: enforce the asserted invariant in the renderer: teamBridgeEventOwnerConsent returns false unless line.targets.length === 1 (preferred), or pluralise the line (ICU plural, which then needs one/few/many/other in ru)
source_findings.reason: the predicate uses .every, and teamBridgeEventLines rolls up same-request_id/same-kind events, so a consent request covering two agents of one owner yields two targets and every locale renders a singular noun with a two-name list ("their agent A and B joining"). No fixture or hub evidence of a multi-target consent event exists, so this is latent, not demonstrated.

source_findings.reason: if a hub ever emits an agent as the consenting actor, "their agent" attributes ownership to an agent; the sidecar says the actor may be an agent, so copy and predicate disagree about what the line may claim.

cross_locale_answer: REUSE OF owner_added_agent: right in all seven, because what transfers is the possessor phrase and each locale rebuilt the verb frame. en drops "own" in both lines ("their agent"), fr/es do the same ("son agent"/"su agente"), while zh ("自己的"), ru ("собственного"), ur ("اپنے"), hi ("अपने") and vi ("của mình") keep the emphatic own-word their sibling uses, so the pairs read in parallel inside each locale. hi/ur had to inflect the possessive to the oblique (अपना->अपने, اپنا->اپنے) for the کو postposition, and did. No locale copied a frame that does not fit "approved ... joining".
